messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | **mosse** | first moment / hour | **घंटा** | “hour” | OK | | **di** (line 40) | genitive “of” | **का** | “of” | OK | | **prima** | “first” (earliest) | — | — | **MISSING** | | **quelle** | demonstrative “those” | **वह** | “that” | OK | | **cose** | “beautiful things” | **मौसम** | “season” (rendered as “sweet season”) | OK | | **belle** | “beautiful / sweet” | **मीठा** | “sweet” | OK | | **sì** | resultative “so, thus” | **ताकि** | “so that” | OK | | **ch'a** | causal “that … to” | **वह … लिये** | “that … for” | OK | | **bene** | “good” | **अच्छी** | “good” | OK | | **sperar** | infinitive “to hope” | **आशा** | “hope” (noun) | OK | | **m'era** | “to me was” (experiencer) | **मेरे** | “my / to me” | OK | | **cagione** | “occasion, cause” | **कारण** | “cause / occasion” | OK | | **di** (line 42) | preposition “of” | **के** | “of” | OK | | **quella** | demonstrative “that” | **उस** | “that” | OK | | **fiera** | “wild beast” | **जंगली जानवर** | “wild animal / beast” | OK | | **a** (line 42) | preposition “to / with” | **के बारे में** | “about / concerning” | OK | | **la** | definite article (fem. sing.) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | **gaetta** | “dappled, speckled” | **धब्बेदार** | “dappled” | OK | | **pelle** | “skin” | **त्वचा** | “skin” | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **MISSING:** *prima* – the notion of “first” is not explicitly expressed in the Hindi translation. - **UNNECESSARY:** *la* – Hindi does not use a definite article; the word is naturally omitted.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 40: - Original: समय का वह घंटा और मीठा मौसम; - Issue: Missing translation of **prima** (“first”). - Corrected: **समय का वह पहला घंटा और मीठा मौसम;**
- Line 41: - Original: तभी वह मेरे लिये अच्छी आशा का कारण बन गया - Issue: Wrong verb form; should express past state “was” rather than “became”. - Corrected: **ताकि वह मेरे लिये अच्छी आशा का कारण था**
- Line 42: - Original: उस जंगली जानवर के बारे में जिसकी धब्बेदार त्वचा थी। - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
``` समय का वह पहला घंटा और मीठा मौसम; ताकि वह मेरे लिये अच्छी आशा का कारण था उस जंगली जानवर के बारे में जिसकी धब्बेदार त्वचा थी। ```
